chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Udhafir, from Abi Hamza or from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

In Kufa there are accursed mosques and blessed mosques … As for the accursed mosques, they are the mosque of Thaqif, the mosque of al-Ash'ath, the mosque of Jarir, the mosque of Simak, and the mosque in al-Khamra which was built on the grave of one Pharaoh among the Pharaohs.
ai.seo_question: Which mosques in Kufa are considered accursed according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the spiritual purity of prayer spaces by distinguishing between mosques blessed by divine favor and those accursed due to historical associations with specific figures or construction on graves. The specific mention of the mosque in al-Khamra being built on the grave of one of the Pharaohs connects the physical location to the Quranic narrative of tyranny and idolatry, while the named mosques (Thaqif, al-Ash'ath, Jarir, Simak) reflect the political and tribal dynamics of early Kufa. This classification serves as a practical guide for worshippers to understand how historical context and physical attributes can influence the spiritual merit of a place of worship.
